plan.title: Kidney treated vs control DE with batch-adjusted DESeq2
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 kidney bulk RNA-seq samples (6 treated vs 6 control) from salmon-derived raw gene counts (12000 genes x 12 samples per metadata, one gene-symbol column in counts.csv), processed in two known batches balanced across condition. Because the batch fully crosses condition, batch is retained as a fixed covariate in the DESeq2 design rather than removed by count adjustment, preserving the negative-binomial mean-variance structure the model relies on. The workflow follows the sourced DESeq2 procedure end-to-end: blind-VST sample-structure QC to confirm the batch does not dominate variance before testing, a minimal count pre-filter, size-factor normalization internal to DESeq2, a ~batch+condition Wald test with an explicit control reference level, apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control coefficient for reporting/ranking, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05 for calling DE genes, and a preranked fgsea enrichment on the Wald statistic against Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways human gene sets available in the reference store. A final report step consolidates diagnostics, the DE gene table (unshrunken and shrunken LFC), and enrichment results with full reproducibility metadata.

steps.method: Minimal pre-filter: >=10 counts in >= smallest group size (6)
DESeq2 design ~ batch + condition, explicit reference level
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald statistic, Hallmark + Reactome + WikiPathways human
Reproducible summary report with diagnostics, gene tables, enrichment tables
